content.rule: Use a sqlite model when the SQLite database is physically or logically separate from the application. For SQLite used as an application-internal cache, create a sqlite_cache entity inside the application model when its acceptable_entities allows sqlite_cache. A .db file or SQLite library alone does not establish a separate model boundary.

separate_database.when: The verified SQLite database is a physically or logically separate storage boundary from the application. A separately managed logical database may reside on the same device.

internal_cache.model: The existing application model; respect its acceptable_entities.
internal_cache.when: SQLite stores cache data inside the application boundary. Model its cache tables as sqlite_cache entities inside that application, including supported Tauri presets.

selection_rules: Determine the database purpose and physical/logical boundary from verified requirements, source or configuration. Do not infer cache semantics from SQLite, a local path or offline persistence alone.
An internal cache does not require a separate sqlite model. A separately managed database remains a sqlite model even when the application also uses it.
Tauri presets remain flat application models. Create a separate sqlite model only for a verified separate database; do not auto-create one for sqlite_cache.
Preserve existing models/entities unless the user authorizes restructuring. This guide does not migrate data or change IDs.
